prediction.likelyOutcome: The right to just compensation is not contested; this case will be decided entirely on valuation. Claimant's $1.7M figure is vulnerable because it rests on a speculative, unapproved two-story redevelopment theory for the NB portion, while the State's $56,825 figure is itself vulnerable because its R-10 residential highest-and-best-use theory is nearly as speculative and its 80% discount ignores claimant's more defensible parking-use theory for that parcel. A trial award meaningfully above the State's number but well below claimant's full ask is the most probable result, with the R-10 parking argument and possible parking-nonconformity consequential damages being claimant's best levers to push the number up.

outcome.description: After a nonjury trial the Court of Claims largely adopted the State's appraisal (rejecting its 80% discount on the R-10 portion), found direct damages of $71,000 ($54,000 NB portion, $17,000 R-10 portion), and entered judgment for the principal sum of $113,730 including other damages not itemized in the decision. The Appellate Division, Second Department affirmed on May 4, 2022.
